stem: Which statement correctly describes the scope of USP General Chapter <797>?

options.A: It describes minimum standards for preparing compounded nonsterile preparations for human and animal use.
options.B: It describes a general quality-assurance framework that applies across pharmaceutical compounding activities.
options.C: It describes minimum standards for preparing compounded sterile preparations for human and animal drugs.
options.D: It describes standards specifically for radiopharmaceutical preparation, compounding, dispensing, and repackaging.

rationale: The current official USP <797> chapter states in its Introduction and Scope that it describes the minimum standards to be followed for preparation of compounded sterile preparations for human and animal drugs. Therefore C is correct. A corresponds to USP <795> on nonsterile preparations. B describes the broader quality-assurance subject addressed by USP <1163>, not the defining scope of <797>. D corresponds to USP <825> for radiopharmaceuticals.
educational_objective: Identify USP <797> as the USP general chapter that establishes minimum standards for compounded sterile preparations for human and animal drugs.
source_version_date: USP-NF official text citation 2025; current page rechecked 2026-08-17
source_locator: Section 1 — Introduction and Scope: minimum standards for preparation of compounded sterile preparations for human and animal drugs
source_claim_supported: USP <797> describes minimum standards for preparation of compounded sterile preparations for human and animal drugs. Official USP pages for <795>, <1163>, and <825> distinguish the distractor chapter scopes.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8/PDF p.12: Apply principles of infection prevention (e.g., hand hygiene, aseptic technique, isolation, sterile technique, universal/standard enhanced barrier precautions)
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — sterile technique and compounded sterile preparations
correction_summary: Narrowed the original patient-safety-purpose item because the current 2025 USP preview directly exposes the chapter's scope but not every detailed harm-prevention claim. Rebuilt the item around the exact current <797> scope and used other official USP chapter scopes (<795>, <1163>, <825>) as plausible distractors. Reduced difficulty from hard to easy.
